title: Consensus of scholars
hook: agreement of the scholars as a source for Sunni schools

segments.voice: Yesterday, the sunnah as second, and your line: the sunnah explains. Did you find someone's example of how a thing is actually done? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-one.

What happens when the people who know a subject best all land in the same place? In Sunni legal thought, that landing place has a name, and it counts as a source of law in its own right, after the Qur'an and the sunnah. Not a vote. Not a poll of the public. The agreement of the community's qualified scholars on a ruling. It sounds simple. Pinning down what it means, whose agreement counts, and how anyone could know it happened, kept scholars arguing. Today: ijma'.
screen: `EVERYONE LANDS IN ONE PLACE.` → `NOT A VOTE.` → `SIMPLE? NOT QUITE.`

segments.voice: First, the word. Ijma' means agreement, a coming together on one thing. In Sunni legal theory it names the agreement of the qualified scholars of the community, in a given generation, on a ruling. Second, the grounds. Scholars point to a report that the Prophet ﷺ said his community would not agree upon error. It comes in more than one collection, in different wordings, and critics have weighed its chains differently. Tradition says al-Shafi'i also pointed to a verse that warns against following a way other than the believers' way. Third, what consensus does. Where it exists, it settles a question. Scholars give examples like the obligation of the daily prayers and the fast of Ramadan, or the gathering of the Qur'an into one written copy that was passed on. And they hold that consensus rests on a text; it doesn't float free of the Qur'an and the sunnah. Fourth, the arguments about agreement itself. Whose agreement counts? Only the companions'? The scholars of any generation? Imam Malik gave special weight to the practice of the people of Medina. Can a consensus even be known, once scholars live scattered across many lands? A saying attributed to Ahmad ibn Hanbal warns that someone who claims consensus may be speaking falsely, since people may have differed without his knowing. And Twelver Shia scholars accept consensus as proof when it reveals the view of the Imam, not as a source standing on its own. So the idea of agreement is itself a place where scholars disagree, carefully, which shows how much weight they gave it.
screen: `IJMA': A COMING TOGETHER.` · `WILL NOT AGREE UPON ERROR.` · `CONSENSUS RESTS ON A TEXT.` · `WHOSE AGREEMENT COUNTS?`

segments.voice: The practice: learn one agreed ruling. Settle, and breathe. Take one that scholars give as an example of consensus: the fast of Ramadan is obligatory. Now picture its reach. People of different schools, different lands, different languages, who differ on a great deal, all keeping the same month. Hold that picture for a few breaths. Then turn it toward your own life. Think of a group you belong to that argues about plenty. What's the one thing nobody in it disputes? Rest there for a moment. The bell holds the time.
Ijma'. Agreement: in Sunni law, the agreement of the community's qualified scholars on a ruling, a source standing after the Qur'an and the sunnah. Today's word.

Your line: agreement. Today, in a conversation where people disagree, find the one thing everyone already agrees on, and say it out loud. Tomorrow: reasoning by analogy. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-one.

howItsDone: Sunni scholars treat a ruling on which the qualified scholars agreed as settled, while Twelver Shia scholars accept consensus when it reflects the view of the Imam; students learn which rulings are held to be agreed and which are differed over.

fork.setup: you're a scholar asked about a question, and you find that the scholars before you agreed on the answer. what do you do?
options: set their agreement aside and start from scratch.
treat the agreement as settling it, and look for the text it rests on.
put the question to a public vote.
fork.reveal: in Sunni legal theory, a real consensus settles the question, and it is expected to rest on a text. the hard part, scholars said, is knowing the agreement was real.

original.note: Arabic: agreement, coming together on one thing; the third source in Sunni legal theory.

trapdoor: what you thought: consensus means everyone agrees, so it's obvious.
what it means: the agreement of qualified scholars on a ruling, a source after the Qur'an and the sunnah in Sunni law.
what a scholar hears: whose agreement counts, and can it be known? Ahmad's warning and the Twelver Shia view show agreement is itself argued over.

sources.ref: Masa'il of Ahmad ibn Hanbal (narrated by his son Abdullah)

notes: 'My community will not agree upon error': Ibn Majah 3950 and Tirmidhi 2167 (wording 'Allah will not gather my ummah upon misguidance'); paraphrased and flagged as weighed differently. Confirm numbers.
Al-Shafi'i's use of Qur'an 4:115 for ijma' is given as 'tradition says' (al-Risala and the story of his search for a proof); confirm.
Examples of consensus (obligation of daily prayers and Ramadan fasting; the companions' agreement on the written mushaf) are standard examples; confirm. No numbers given.
'Consensus rests on a text' (the requirement of a mustanad) stated as what scholars hold; a Keeper may want 'most scholars'.
Malik and the practice ('amal) of Medina: described as 'special weight', not as ijma' proper; confirm the framing.
Ahmad's saying ('whoever claims consensus is lying; perhaps people differed') is attributed, paraphrased, and softened to 'may be speaking falsely'. Confirm source.
Twelver Shia view of ijma' as kashif (revealing the Imam's view): confirm wording. The outline's hook says 'a source for Sunni schools'; the Shia view is added for fairness.
Original: إجماع; pronunciation given as 'ij-MAA' (final 'ayn not marked); confirm.

Editor: the practice example changed from the daily prayers to the Ramadan fast (both are named in the teach), since 1169 and 1170 already center on prayer; stock phrase 'turned out to be anything but' replaced.
